newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam targets social vice in old Saigon.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam targets social vice in old Saigon.

text.p: Vietnam said on Saturday it had renewed a drive against social evils in freewheeling Ho Chi Minh City, the capital of former South Vietnam.

State-controlled media reported that city authorities had launched a three-week clampdown on establishments seen as a breeding ground for vice, including massage parlours, karaoke bars, video shops and games centres.
"Those found to be running illegal practices will receive strict punishments from the local government," the English-language Vietnam news said.

Vietnam's battle against social evils, once defined as prostitution, gambling and drug-abuse, was relaunched with spectacular vigour earlier this year in the run-up to a major Communist Party congress.

Teams of police workers tore across cities covering up, painting over or ripping down billboards emblazoned with foreign-brand names. Videos, CDs and "culturally polluting" magazines were ritually destroyed.
In recent months, however, the campaign had been toned down.
Government officials say the aim is to protect Vietnamese culture from harmful influences, many of which are seen as originating abroad.
